column1: # Why an allocation-relevant owned branch outcome stays uncovered.
# Columns (tab-separated): file regex, line range (a-b, or * for the whole file), reason.
# The first matching rule wins. `discovery.py manifest --strict` fails on an unmatched outcome.
# Line numbers follow the source: run `manifest` again after an edit and update the ranges.

column3: Zero-size request: the arenas never request 0 bytes (each string or item has a header).
Zero-size request: the arenas never request 0 bytes (each string or item has a header).
Linear chunk exhausted: `ChainAllocator` sizes each new chunk for the request, so a chunk it just made always fits. Arena exhaustion is injected one level up (`ArenaRequest`/`ArenaBacking`).
Zero-size or over-page-aligned request: the arenas ask for page-aligned chunks of at least one item.
Zero-size request: never made by `ChainAllocator`.
`mmap` failure: the harness injects arena failures above `VirtualAllocator` (`ArenaBacking`), which return the same `AllocError` this branch returns.
`ArrayQueue` is not part of the profiling API the .NET profiler calls (target APIs: profile new/add/serialize/reset, endpoint and upscaling metadata, exporter new/send, drops).
`ddog_StringWrapper_drop` belongs to the managed string storage API, not a target API.
Azure App Services variables are absent on the test host, so no entry matches. Reading `/proc/self/environ` (the allocations before this test) is reached and failed by the `Exporter_new` scenarios.
The process-wide lazy machine id is never requested on the paths of the target APIs, so the normalization never runs.
File endpoint dump server. The exporter scenarios use a local HTTP agent instead, because the dump server leaks a socket per run in `/tmp` (step 5 finding).
`ddog_CancellationToken_clone` is not called: the .NET profiler sends without a cancellation token (the scenarios pass null).
`ProfileError` belongs to the profiles dictionary API (`ProfileStatus` results), not to the target APIs, which return `ddog_Error`.
`ProfileStatus` belongs to the profiles dictionary API, not a target API.
Lossy UTF-8 conversion serves the dictionary and cxx APIs. `ddog_prof_Profile_add` takes UTF-8 `CharSlice`s.
`From<&Location>` for the prost types: used by the protobuf tests and benches, not by serialization.
Managed string storage (`get_seq_num`): not a target API.
Azure App Services metadata is absent on the test host. With it, `Exporter_new` would reserve and push more tags: a gap of the test environment, not of the API sequence.
`try_add_sample2` (`ddog_prof_Profile_add2`, dictionary API): not a target API.
`add_string_id_sample` (managed string ids): not a target API.
`experimental_omit_local_root_span_id_when_serializing` has no FFI setter, so the C API never takes this branch.
String-id sample validation: not reached by a target API.
`api2` label validation (`ddog_prof_Profile_add2`): not a target API.
Profiles dictionary translation (`ddog_prof_Profile_add2`): not a target API.
By-value upscaling rule (empty label name and value). Gap: the sequence generator never produces an empty label name, so neither the scenarios nor the fuzzer register one. Follow-up for step 8.
Parallel sharded sets back the profiles dictionary, not a target API.
`needs_drop::<T>()` is a constant per item type, and the item types reached here need no drop.
Spare capacity too small: callers size the spare capacity with the same layout first.
Compressed output over `max_capacity` (the encoded profile size cap): the largest scenario stays far below it.
